newsitem.title: GERMANY: International investors show an interest in Bewag.
newsitem.headline: International investors show an interest in Bewag.

text.p: International investors have displayed a strong interest in buying shares in the mainly state-owned utility, Berlin Kraft und Licht AG (Bewag), which is set to be privatised, the company said on Sunday.

Bewag's chief executive Dietmar Winje told journalists at a breakfast briefing that 28 investors from abroad had expressed an interest so far and that Bewag was interested in completing the sale to allow it to remain an independent power supplier.
The city-state of Berlin said late in October that it would sell its remaining 50.8 percent of shares in Bewag, adding it expected revenues of around 5.7 billion marks ($3.75 billion) from the sale.
Winje said that sales in the first 10 months of 1996 2.79 billion marks and that the company planned to reduce costs by at least 500 million marks annually over the next five years.

Bewag was considering taking stakes in other companies and was also examining markets in the Czech Republic, Poland and the Baltic states, Winje said. He also ruled out the possibility of the group moving into nuclear energy.
In common with other utilities, Winje said that Bewag was interested in developing in the telecommunications area and was seeking a partner to this end.
From the beginning of 1997, Bewag plans to drop its electricity prices by five percent.
Other shareholders in Bewag include the Viag AG unit Bayernwerk and Veba AG's PreussenElektra, with 10 percent each. The remaining shares are spread among smaller shareholders.
